messages:
anya: quick thread  we need a concrete playbook for schema upgrades that covers routing, provenance, and cost attribution. three knobs on table: 1) header-based fastpath (clients stamp schema) 2) edge-normalizer that does lightweight renames/validation 3) registry-driven heavy transforms (signed wasm packs). leaning header-first + registry for heavy lifts. thoughts?
rob: header-first reduces runtime work a lot. must define header name + semantics (suggest X-RI-Schema-Version). important: if header absent, we must run normalization but keep original envelope intact for audits.
jing: auditability is critical. if we mutate we should store canonicalized output and the raw envelope both (or store a delta). that lets us attribute downstream costs to the normalized footprint while retaining raw for replay. storage cost is a policy decision.
sam: agree. for cost attribution we need deterministic post-transform tokens for per-tenant billing. transforms must output stable billing keys (billing.service, billing.env). registry bundles should declare which billing keys they produce. provenance-bot: declared billing keys for bundle=bundle-2026-04-01: [billing.service,billing.env].
anya: operational constraints: edge-normalizer should only do cheap ops (renames, enum normalizing). anything that needs compute or logic should call transform-service with signed wasm. edge-normalizer must never execute arbitrary bundles.
rob: fallback plan: if transform-service is unhealthy, we buffer raw envelopes to obs-replay topic and mark tenant with migration_state=blocked. ops-bot: obs-replay enqueue accepted id=or-362468-01.
jing: we also need a "replay & reconcile" tool so SDK owners can replay buffered raw envelopes through a target transform to validate output before flipping clients. CLI example:
```
# replay buffered events through a transform bundle locally
obs-replay --bundle bundle-2026-04-01 --input obs-backlog/2026-04-01.ndjson --out ./replayed.json
```
anya: good. security: registry must sign wasm bundles and we verify signatures at load. also record audit events when a bundle mutates billing keys. manifest: require two approvals to publish a registry bundle.
sam: migration gating: 1) add header parsing + fastpath routing 2) deploy edge-normalizer (non-mutating mode for 2wk shadow), 3) launch registry + transform-service + signed bundles 4) run shadow transforms 0.1%->1%->5%->25% with divergence checks 5) open opt-in for tenants to have transforms applied 6) after 3mo of low divergence, require header or remove shim.
rob: canary metrics: header_fraction, shadow_divergence_pct (hash compare), transform_latency_p50/p95, billing_key_stability_pct, transform_cpu_seconds_by_tenant. keep retention 180d.
jing: tooling: obs-compat-check CLI for SDKs to run in CI. sample output:
```
obs-compat-check --schema schemas/v5.json --samples ./smoke.json --staging https://staging-edge.internal
# output: header-ready: 73%; missing billing.env in 6.2% (120 events); suggested mapping: env->billing.env
```
anya: billing policy: Hosted covers translation CPU for a 6 month migration window. after that, tenants that rely on server-side transforms can choose a paid option or self-host transform-service in private/dedicated. finance to confirm pricing.
sam: need tenant flag: "schema_mode": ["auto-transform","require-header","self-hosted"], default auto-transform for hosted tenants created before cutoff-date. add an account-level opt-out flow.
rob: owners: anya (product), rob (routing + header spec), jing (provenance + replay tooling), sam (billing + transform infra). ops-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/obs-upgrade-playbook-3624689999 (assigned anya).
anya: I'll draft the RFC with examples, migration timeline, and required dashboards. please ack by EOD. :mag_right:
rob: ack.
jing: ack.
sam: ack.
provenance-bot: replay manifest created: replay-job-362468-01 (owner: jing).
